rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians take the lām as eventual outcome, reconciling punishment with 51:56's stated purpose of creating jinn and humans to worship.
rows.anchor: وإنما احتاج هذا القائل إلى كونها لام العاقبة لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses lām for an eventual outcome in the example about giving birth for death and building for ruin.
rows.anchor: 2344 لدوا للموت وابنوا للخراب

rows.speaker: الآخر
rows.claim: A second unnamed poet likewise says every newborn is born for death, illustrating the eventual-outcome lām.
rows.anchor: 2345 ألا كل مولود فللموت يولد

rows.speaker: الآخر
rows.claim: A third unnamed poet illustrates the same outcome sense: mothers raise young for death and houses are built for ruin.
rows.anchor: 2346 فللموت تغذو الوالدات سخالها

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the lām causal figuratively, since their eventual destination is Hell and is treated as the cause.
rows.anchor: أنها للعلة وذلك أنهم لما كان مآلهم إليها جعل ذلك سببا على طريق المجاز

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the outcome-lām analysis because the act here was intended to result in their dwelling in Hell.
rows.anchor: لام العاقبة إنما تتصور إذا كان فعل الفاعل لم يقصد مصير الأمر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the outcome reading, the lām attaches to ذرأنا.
rows.anchor: واللام على هذا متعلقة ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may instead attach to an omitted element, making it a circumstantial modifier of كثيرا, originally its delayed adjective.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to posit inversion to mean that God created Hell for many; that construction is only necessary or rare.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى ادعاء قلب وأن الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الجن is an adjective modifying كثيرا.
rows.anchor: و { من الجن } صفة ل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لهم قلوب is a clause in the accusative, analyzable as an adjective or circumstantial clause for كثيرا or for the pronoun carried by من الجن.
rows.anchor: جملة في محل نصب: إما صفة لكثير أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is preferable to take لهم alone as the adjective or circumstantial phrase, with قلوب as its subject and a single-word description.
rows.anchor: على حدته هو الوصف أو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses لا يفقهون بها and its parallel are adjectival clauses; this qualification is nearly indispensable to make the description informative.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الجملة المنفية في محل النعت لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger analysis makes الحسنى the feminine of أحسن; nonrational broken plurals may take feminine adjectives, while masculine matching is also possible.
rows.anchor: والجمع المكسر لغير العاقل يجوز أن يوصف بما يوصف

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic example supports the alternative that الحسنى is a verbal noun on the fuʿlā pattern, like الرجعى and البقيا.
rows.anchor: 2347 ولا يجزون من حسنى بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأسماء here means the words that designate God, such as Allah and al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: الألفاظ الدالة على الباري تعالى كالله والرحمن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the intended meaning is the names' designations by consensus; the author objects that a verbal noun is not what one invokes.
rows.anchor: المراد بها التسميات إجماعا من المتأولين لا يمكن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the author's preferred explanation of دعوه, it means call upon God by these names, as in calling Him Allah or al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: نادوه بها، كقولهم: يا الله يا رحمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes فادعوه as name Him with these names, like naming a son Zayd.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سموه بها كقولك: " سميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads يلحدون with open yāʾ and ḥāʾ from the triliteral لحد; the other readers use ʾalḥada with a damma and kasra.
rows.anchor: يلحدون بفتح الياء والحاء من لحد ثلاثيا

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt treats the two readings as synonymous, both meaning to incline or deviate, and glosses them as turning away from truth.
rows.anchor: وإلى كونهما بمعنى واحد ذهب ابن السكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun لحد is connected with the grave niche because it is dug to one side, unlike a central الضريح.
rows.anchor: ومنه لحد القبر لأنه يمال

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet's use of الملحد illustrates that أَلحد is more common in usage than لحد.
rows.anchor: وألحد أكثر استعمالا من لحد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes the roots: لحد means to lean or take refuge, while ألحد means to incline or deviate; he also reports ألحد as turn away and لحد as lean.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: " لحد بمعنى ركن وانضوى، وألحد: مال وانحرف " قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda transmits from al-Aṣmaʿī that ألحد means dispute or argue, whereas لحد means turn aside or lean.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو عبيدة عن الأصمعي: " ألحد: مارى وجادل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading with ألحد is favored by agreement with the Qurʾanic wording بإلحاد.
rows.anchor: ورجحت قراءة العامة بالإجماع على قوله

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Arabs scarcely use the active participle لاحد; the author says its rarity is shown by this absence but notes the attested phrase لحده اللاحد.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي: " ولا يكاد يسمع من العرب لاحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād may mean deriving idols' names from God's names, such as al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.
rows.anchor: أن اشتقوا منها أسماء لآلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ilḥād may mean attributing to God names that do not befit His majesty.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد سموه بما لا يليق بجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction كدأب آل has an analogue previously discussed in Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم نظيره في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك بأن is analyzed as a subject and predicate, as in its parallel: that punishment or requital is because God did not change a blessing until people changed themselves.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر أيضا كنظيره، أي: ذلك العذاب أو الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers open the hamza of وأن الله, coordinating it with the preceding أن and giving the sense that God's hearing and knowledge are another cause; a kasra reading begins a new sentence.
rows.anchor: أي: وسبب أن الله سميع عليم. ويقرأ بكسرها على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من أنفسكم adjectivally modifies رسول and means he is from the heart of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: صفة لرسول، أي: من صميم العرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on fāʾ, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and several others, means from your noblest or most choice people; it is also attributed to the Prophet, Fāṭima, and ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: أي: من أشرفكم، من النفاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes عزيز an adjective of رسول; ما is either a verbal noun or relative pronoun and is the subject of عزيز, meaning your hardship grieves him.
rows.anchor: صفة لرسول، وفيه أنه تقدم غير الوصف الصريح

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet's example يسر المرء ما ذهب الليالي supports reading the ما-clause as the subject of عزيز, like the nights' passing being what gladdens a person.
rows.anchor: 2557 يسر المرء ما ذهب الليالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes عزيز a fronted predicate and ما عنتم a delayed subject, with the whole clause describing the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " عزيز " خبرا مقدما

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī proposes عزيز as subject and ما عنتم as its predicate, despite the indefinite subject's following prepositional complement.
rows.anchor: وجوز الحوفي أن يكون " عزيز " مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers عزيز as an adjective of رسول because حريص is also adjectival; positing an omitted هو before حريص is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: صفة لرسول؛ لقوله بعد ذلك " حريص " فلم يجعل خبرا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بالمؤمنين attaches to رؤوف.
rows.anchor: و " بالمؤمنين " متعلق برؤوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is not syntactic competition between two governors because that requires the shared complement to follow both; some grammarians nevertheless allow examples such as ضربت وشتمته.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون المسألة من التنازع لأن من شرطه تأخر المعمول عن العاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this analysis is nevertheless weakened into competition, the second verb governs because making the first govern would require an omitted object in the second.
rows.anchor: أنه متى أعمل الأول أضمر في الثاني من غير حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعواهم is the subject and سبحانك is the predicate, supplied by an unspoken verb; their invocation is this expression.
rows.anchor: معمول لفعل مقدر لا يجوز إظهاره هو الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعوى can mean invocation, supported by اللهم as a vocative meaning يا الله.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه " اللهم " لأنه نداء في معنى يا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعوى may instead mean worship, with the verbal noun annexed to its agent.
rows.anchor: أن يكون هذا الدعاء هنا بمعنى العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On verbal ascription, their prayer in Paradise is this quoted formula; on semantic ascription, they say this and all equivalent expressions of transcendence, as with 2:58.
rows.anchor: بل يقولونه وما يؤدي معناه من جميع صفات التنزيه والتقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحيتهم is a subject and سلام its predicate; the verbal noun may be annexed to its agent, meaning they greet one another with peace.
rows.anchor: خبرها، وهو كالذي قبله، والمصدر هنا يحتمل أن يكون مضافا لفاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the greeting noun is annexed to its recipient, meaning angels greet them, supported by 13:23.
rows.anchor: تحيتهم التي تحييهم بها الملائكة سلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيها in both places attaches to the preceding verbal noun.
rows.anchor: في الموضعين متعلق بالمصدر قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word قبل may be a circumstantial phrase modifying what follows through an omitted element, though the author does not favor this parse.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا مما بعده فيتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow تحيتهم to be annexed simultaneously to agent and recipient, greeting one another; they compare the dual relation in the judgment of David and Solomon at 21:78.
rows.anchor: مما أضيف فيه المصدر لفاعله ومفعوله معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simultaneous annexation depends on whether one allows combining literal and figurative meaning; if not, its proponents answer that the minimum plural is two, hence لحكمهم.
rows.anchor: هل يجوز الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آخر دعواهم is the subject; أن is the lightened form of الثقيلة with an omitted pronoun of شأن as subject and the following nominal clause as predicate.
rows.anchor: هي المخففة من الثقيلة، واسمها ضمير الأمر والشأن حذف

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem supplies an example of the lightened أن followed by a clause expressing that everyone who walks barefoot or shod will perish.
rows.anchor: 2573 في فتية كسيوف الهند قد علموا

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjānī claims أن is extra and construes the phrase as وآخر دعواهم الحمد لله; the author says this lacks evidence and conflicts with Sībawayh and the grammarians.
rows.anchor: والتقدير: وآخر دعواهم الحمد لله، وهي دعوى لا دليل عليها

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad claims that lightened أن can still govern just as the geminated form does.
rows.anchor: المخففة يجوز إعمالها مخففة كهي مشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading lightens أن and puts الحمد in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وتخفيف " أن " ورفع " الحمد " هو

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima and the named readers instead geminate أن and put the dāl of الحمد in the accusative as its noun; this confirms the common reading's lightened construction and refutes al-Jurjānī.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب بتشديدها ونصب دال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading annexes كل to زوجين, while Ḥafṣ reads كل with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: قرأ العامة بإضافة " كل " لزوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the common reading, اثنين may be the object of احمل and من كل زوجين a circumstantial phrase from that object, originally its adjective moved ahead.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من المفعول لأنه كان صفة للنكرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse treats من as extra, كل as the object, and اثنين as an emphatic adjective of زوجين; this requires accepting extra من in general or in affirmative clauses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل " من " زائدة، و " كل " مفعول به

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī and others take زوجين as a generic expression for everything that has a pair.
rows.anchor: بمعنى العموم أي: من كل ما له ازدواج

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues that taking the phrase as two already existing members of every pair would require carrying four of every kind; in ordinary usage a pair is one member of a pair.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " ولو كان المعنى: احمل فيها من كل زوجين حاصلين اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ḥafṣ's tanwīn reading, من كل حيوان is meant, زوجين is the object, and اثنين emphatically modifies it.
rows.anchor: فمعناها من كل حيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ḥafṣ's reading, من كل may attach directly to احمل, as is apparent, or be an omitted modifier in the circumstantial phrase from زوجين.
rows.anchor: وهو الظاهر، وأن يتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same parsing dispute applies at 23:27.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخلاف والتخريج جاريان أيضا في سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأهلك coordinates with اثنين in the reading that annexes كل to زوجين, and with زوجين in the tanwīn reading.
rows.anchor: نسق على " اثنين " في قراءة من أضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا من سبق is a connected exception in an affirmative clause, and by the standard rule must be accusative.
rows.anchor: استثناء متصل في موجب، فهو واجب النصب على المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ومن آمن is another object of احمل, coordinated with its first object.
rows.anchor: مفعول به نسقا على مفعول " احمل "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of وقال may be Noah, or God speaking to Noah and those with him.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الفاعل ضمير نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيها attaches to اركبوا; the preposition في is used because the verb implies enter while riding or travel within it.
rows.anchor: وعدي ب " في " لتضمنه معنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One proposed estimate is اركبوا الماء فيها.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: اركبوا الماء فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis treats في as extra for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقيل: " في " زائدة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بسم الله may be a circumstantial phrase from the subject of اركبوا or the pronoun in فيها; مجراها and مرساها then function as subjects of the implied stability in that phrase.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا الجار والمجرور حالا من فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, بسم الله is a fronted predicate and مجراها a delayed subject, with the sentence as an estimated circumstantial clause, as Abū al-Baqāʾ and others parse it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " بسم الله " خبرا مقدما

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī objects that these circumstantial parses lack a linking pronoun returning to the subject of اركبوا; the pronoun in بسم الله links to مجراها, or to فيها under the relevant parse.
rows.anchor: إلا أن مكيا منع ذلك لخلو الجملة من ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes بسم الله circumstantial and treats مجراها and مرساها as spatial or temporal adverbs: embark naming the location or time of sailing and mooring.
rows.anchor: في موضع الظرف المكاني أو الزماني

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says the adverbs' governing element is the implied stability in بسم الله, so the meaning is to embark invoking God's blessing at those places or times.
rows.anchor: والعامل في هذين الظرفين حينئذ ما تضمنه

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī rules out اركبوا as the adverbs' governor: the command is to name God at sailing and mooring, not to embark during those times.
rows.anchor: قال مكي: " ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مجراها and مرساها may be verbal nouns raised by بسم الله as subjects, meaning their launching and mooring occur through God's name; then بسم الله can only be circumstantial from the pronoun in فيها.
rows.anchor: مصدرين، و " بسم الله " حال كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With those parses the utterance is one sentence; it may instead be an independent clause about the vessel's movement and stopping being by God's name.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة لا تعلق لها بالأولى من حيث الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted interpretation says the ship stopped when he said بسم الله and moved when he said it intending to sail; both clauses are quoted under وقال.
rows.anchor: وقفت، وإذا قالها جرت عند إرادته ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two Ḥijāzī readers and Ḥafṣ open the mīm of مجراها; the others use a damma.
rows.anchor: بفتح الميم والباقون بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven readers agree on a damma in مرساها, while Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Zayd b. ʿAlī, and al-Aʿmash read its mīm open.
rows.anchor: واتفق السبعة على ضم ميم " مرساها "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damma readings derive from أجرى and أرسى, while the fatha readings derive from جرت and رست; either can be a time or place adverb or a verbal noun under the earlier parses.
rows.anchor: فالضم فيهما لأنهما من أجرى وأرسى، والفتح لأنهما من جرت ورست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and other readers use the active participles مجريها and مرسيها, parsed as appositions to the name of God.
rows.anchor: وهما اسما فاعلين من أجرى وأرسى، وتخريجهما

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ, and Makkī call these active participles adjectives of God; the author says this only works if the annexation becomes definite, which conflicts with al-Khalīl's rule for صفة مشبهة.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وأبو البقاء ومكي: إنهما نعتان لله تعالى

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says they can instead stand in place of active participles as estimated circumstantial modifiers in the accusative from God's name; he calls this a difficult, notable problem.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي: " ولو جعلت " مجراها " و " مرساها " في موضع اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهي تجري may be an independent clause, a circumstantial clause from the hidden pronoun in بسم الله, or a circumstantial clause from an omitted element inferred from context.
rows.anchor: في هذه الجملة ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies the context: they embarked saying بسم الله, and the vessel was then moving with them.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسره الزمخشري بقوله: " أي: تجري وهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بهم may attach to تجري.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { بهم } يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يتعلق ب " تجري "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, بهم attaches to an omitted element, meaning the vessel moves while carrying them.
rows.anchor: أي: تجري ملتبسة بهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses تجري بهم as meaning that they are aboard the vessel.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسره الزمخشري بقوله: " أي: تجري وهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرسو means becoming fixed and settled, from رسا يرسو and أرسيتُه.
rows.anchor: والرسو: الثبات والاستقرار، يقال: رسا يرسو وأرسيته أنا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses ترسو to mean that a steadfast soul settles while a coward's soul stirs.
rows.anchor: ترسو إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قدم and أورد may compete to govern النار with an implied إلى; the second is applied with deletion, while applying the first would require an omitted complement in the second.
rows.anchor: بحرف الجر، أي: يقدم قومه إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أورد has no syntactic position as a new sentence; it is past in form but future in meaning because it coordinates with an explicitly future verb.
rows.anchor: وهو ماض لفظا مستقبل معنى؛ لأنه عطف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some explain the past form as expressing an event whose occurrence is certain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أوقع الماضي هنا لتحققه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the past literally: Pharaoh already brought them to the Fire in this world, as in 40:46.
rows.anchor: وهذا قد وقع وانفصل وذلك أنه أوردهم في الدنيا النار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation says he brought them the causes of the Fire; the author finds this strained because of the coordination with فاء.
rows.anchor: أسبابها، وفيه بعد لأجل العطف بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الورد can be the verbal noun of arrival, the thing brought, or the one arriving.
rows.anchor: يكون مصدرا بمعنى الورود، ويكون بمعنى الشيء المورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الورد means arrival or an arriving person, an omitted place is needed: the place of the arrival destined to be the Fire, since subject and specific referent of نعم and بئس must agree.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من حذف مضاف تقديره: وبئس مكان الورد المورود

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allow المورود to modify الورد, with النار as an omitted specific referent of blame; this matches the apparent reading of al-Zamakhsharī.
rows.anchor: والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره: بئس الورد المورود النار

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Shaykh proposes الورد as the whole arriving people and المورود as their adjective, with the omitted specific referent being هم; the author questions the internal consistency of that analysis.
rows.anchor: كذا قاله الشيخ. وفيه نظر لا يخفى

rows.speaker: ابن السراج
rows.claim: Grammarians disagree over whether the adjective may modify the specific referent of نعم and بئس; Ibn al-Sarrāj and Abū ʿAlī prohibit it.
rows.anchor: منعه ابن السراج وأبو علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read يرجع as passive; the remaining readers use the active voice.
rows.anchor: مبنيا للمفعول، والباقون مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ address the hearers in تعملون to match اعملوا; the other readers use third person referring back to الذين لا يؤمنون, also at the end of 27.
rows.anchor: بالخطاب لأن قبله " اعملوا " والباقون بالغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis returns له to the repeated من and understands the verse as describing groups of angels who follow one another for those who speak secretly or openly.
rows.anchor: لمن أسر القول ولمن جهر به ولمن استخفى وسرب معقبات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās returns له to the second من; Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains the guardians as a man's guards and retinue, concerning unbelieving leaders, a choice also attributed to al-Ṭabarī and others.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس. قال ابن عطية

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī says the interpretation is negative, with an implied لا: they do not guard him.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الماوردي ذكر على التأويل أن الكلام نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Māwardī's implied negation because a positive clause cannot simply mean a negative one; omission of لا is only licensed in a jussive response to an oath, as at 12:85.
rows.anchor: وهذا ينبغي أن [لا] يسمع البتة، كيف يبرز كلام موجب

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī instead says they guard him, as he supposes and believes, from God's command.
rows.anchor: كما قال المهدوي -يحفظونه من أمر الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A third analysis returns له to God and يحفظونه to the servant: angels guard the servant from harm and record his deeds; this is attributed to al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: ويحفطون عليه أعماله، قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis returns both pronouns to the Prophet despite no nearby mention, since he was implied earlier in 6:8.
rows.anchor: الرابع: عود الضميرين على النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معقبات is the plural of معقب from ʿaqaba, either because angels succeed one another or because they follow what is spoken.
rows.anchor: جمع " معقب " بزنة مفعل، من عقب الرجل إذا جاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the original form was معتقبات with tā assimilated into qāf, comparing it to المعذرون.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والأصل معتقبات، فأدغمت التاء في القاف

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Shaykh calls the assimilation explanation a grave error: tā and qāf do not assimilate in either direction, and the cited المعذرون need not derive from المعتذرون.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وهذا وهم فاحش لا تدغم التاء في القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed kasra reading معقبات relies on the same untenable derivation from متعقبات.
rows.anchor: بكسر العين ولم يقرأ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معقبة may mean معقب with an intensive tāʾ and then take a plural, or it may be a feminine adjective for a group that is itself pluralized.
rows.anchor: والتاء للمبالغة كعلامة ونسابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, معقبة may be an adjective for a group, then pluralized as that description.
rows.anchor: صفة لجماعة، ثم جمع هذا الوصف

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr calls معقبة a plural of معقب, comparing it to رجل، رجال، رجالات.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن جرير أن " معقبة " جمع معقب

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects that morphological analogy: the relevant pattern is جمل، جمال، جمالات, while معقبة and معقبات follow ضاربة and ضاربات.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس كما ذكر، إنما ذلك كجمل وجمال وجمالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reconciles Ibn Jarīr as describing usage, where a feminine form applies to a group, like الواردة; broken plurals of rational beings also take feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: أنه أطلق من حيث الاستعمال على جمع معقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Broken plurals of rational beings take feminine agreement, as shown by the cited examples; Ibn Jarīr's comparison is semantic, not morphological.
rows.anchor: أن جموع التكسير في العقلاء تعامل معاملة المؤنثة

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy, Ibrāhīm, and ʿUbayd Allāh b. Ziyād read له معاقيب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وإبراهيم وعبيد الله بن زياد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives معاقيب from معقب or معقبة, with yāʾ replacing one deleted qāf in the broken plural.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: [جمع معقب أو] معقبة، والياء عوض من حذف

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī analyzes معاقيب as the broken plural of معقب like مطعم/مطاعيم, with yāʾ replacing the deleted tāʾ marbūṭa.
rows.anchor: ما قاله ابن جني فإنه قال: " معاقيب تكسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من بين يديه may modify معقبات, attach directly to it with من marking origin, or be a circumstantial phrase from the pronoun in the locative predicate; each parse completes the clause at ومن خلفه.
rows.anchor: من بين يديه } يجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ's compressed wording means the same three parses and likewise finishes the clause at ومن خلفه.
rows.anchor: وعبر أبو البقاء عن هذه الأوجه بعبارة مشكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead attach to يحفظونه, describing protection from in front and behind; the following repeated من differs in meaning, resolving the apparent duplicate-governor problem.
rows.anchor: متحدان لفظا ومعنى بعامل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يحفظونه may be an adjective of معقبات or a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in the locative predicate.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون صفة ل " معقبات "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من أمر الله may mean because of God's command; a reading by ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd b. ʿAlī, and ʿIkrima with بأمر الله supports this.
rows.anchor: ويدل له قراءة علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وزيد بن علي وعكرمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the causal reading, some say the angels preserve the servant's deeds by God's leave, with a noun omitted.
rows.anchor: يحفظون عمله بإذن الله، فحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes من in its basic sense of origin, construing أمر الله as the jinn and humans from whom protection is needed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " من أمر الله، أي: من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking من as عن has no meaning appropriate to the verse.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن تكون بمعنى " عن " ، وليس عليه معنى يليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من أمر الله may modify an omitted noun describing معقبات, producing several permissible adjectival descriptions; no fronting or inversion is needed, contrary to al-Farrāʾ and others.
rows.anchor: وليس في الكلام تقديم وتأخير كما زعم الفراء وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing word for إذا is omitted, recoverable from its response as لم يرد or وقع; the response after فاء cannot govern backward.
rows.anchor: ولا يعمل فيها جوابها؛ لأن ما بعد الفاء لا يعمل فيما قبلها
